news.title: Tesla's Houston Robotaxi Map Includes 'Fake' Service Areas
news.summary: Tesla's new Robotaxi service in Houston has been criticized for including areas where the service is not actually available, according to a former Tesla employee.
news.body:
Tesla's new Rocket-shaped Robotaxi service area in Houston includes parts of downtown where the service won't actually pick up passengers, according to Ethan McKanna, the creator of Robotaxi Tracker and a former Tesla employee. McKanna rode the service after Monday's expansion and described Houston as the most egregious example of a 'fake' autonomous vehicle (AV) service area he has seen.

The service area was expanded into the shape of a rocket, stretching from a small launch zone in northwest Harris County down to downtown and Bellaire. However, McKanna found that the app would not allow pickups in certain parts of downtown Houston, despite being within the advertised service area. In one instance, he spent about 40 minutes traveling just two blocks due to an unusual route that avoided railroad crossings.

McKanna acknowledged that AV service area maps are often not entirely accurate, but he criticized Tesla for prioritizing the rocket shape over actual service availability. He noted that Tesla's approach contrasts with Waymo, which recently had a smaller gap in its service area that is likely to be addressed soon.

Despite the issues, McKanna praised the overall Robotaxi experience in Houston, noting reasonable wait times and better driving performance compared to other services. However, he emphasized that service and product should always take precedence over marketing, and Tesla's approach in this case falls short.

Robotaxi Tracker remains a key independent source for tracking Tesla's Robotaxi fleet and service areas, providing transparency in an industry where companies often do not share detailed data.

news.title: xAI buys Mississippi homes to avoid data center noise lawsuit
news.summary: xAI is reportedly buying homes in Mississippi in exchange for residents not joining a lawsuit over noise from its data center and power plant.
news.body:
xAI, a company led by Elon Musk, is reportedly purchasing homes in Southaven, Mississippi, in exchange for residents agreeing not to join a lawsuit against the company. The move involves a subsidiary of xAI, MZX, which is offering to buy hundreds of homes in the area. According to reports, the company is targeting 418 homes, with 18 already under consideration for sale. The real estate offers come with a condition: homeowners must sign a release agreement that bars them from pursuing claims related to the lawsuit, including any damages or legal relief from the ongoing case.

The lawsuit was filed by three residents who claim that xAI's data center and gas-fired turbines are causing constant noise and vibrations. The company has been expanding its data center operations in the region, including the construction of two large facilities in Memphis and a power plant in Southaven. This expansion has drawn increasing public and political scrutiny, particularly as opposition to AI data centers grows ahead of the midterm elections.

The Mississippi Free Press reported that residents received letters from MZX offering to buy their homes in exchange for a release of claims related to the lawsuit. The letters emphasized that signing the agreement would prevent individuals from bringing any claims against the company in the future. This strategy appears to be part of a broader effort by xAI to manage legal challenges and continue its infrastructure development in the area.

xAI is also facing legal action from the NAACP, which alleges that the company is operating unpermitted methane gas turbines in Southaven. A federal judge recently blocked an attempt by the Trump administration to dismiss the lawsuit, highlighting the growing legal challenges facing the company.

news.title: Flexell Space and Satoro to Test Solar Cells on SpaceX Falcon 9 Missions
news.summary: Flexell Space and Satoro have agreed to collaborate on in-orbit demonstrations of next-generation space solar cells, with launches planned aboard SpaceX Falcon 9 rockets in 2027 and 2028.
news.body:
Flexell Space, a space energy company based in Korea, has partnered with Singapore-based CubeSat specialist Satoro to conduct in-orbit demonstrations of next-generation space solar cells. The collaboration involves two demonstration missions, one in 2027 and another in 2028, both to be launched aboard SpaceX Falcon 9 rockets. These missions aim to validate the performance and reliability of Flexell Space’s solar cells in the actual space environment.

Flexell Space previously conducted two space demonstration missions using Korea’s KSLV-II rocket in 2025 and 2026. This new agreement with Satoro will expand opportunities for in-orbit validation of its next-generation solar cells and support the accumulation of operational data needed for commercialization. Satoro will be responsible for manufacturing the satellites, while Flexell Space will supply the solar cells and test modules.

The collaboration combines Satoro’s expertise in CubeSat manufacturing and demonstration missions with Flexell Space’s capabilities in developing next-generation solar cell technologies. Flexell Space is focusing on CIGS (copper indium gallium selenide) and perovskite-based solar cells, aiming to provide low-cost, large-area, ultralight power solutions for satellites and space infrastructure.

The data collected from these missions will be used to compare ground-test results with in-orbit performance, assess power output characteristics, and evaluate long-term performance changes. This will support further design improvements and reliability validation, strengthening the technical foundation for evaluations by global customers and future commercial supply.

Flexell Space’s CEO, Taehun Ahn, emphasized the importance of securing in-orbit data to validate the performance and reliability of their solar cells. He noted that the collaboration with Satoro will establish a clear path from development to in-orbit demonstration, accelerating preparations for future commercial supply.

news.title: Tesla confirms Vietnam entry to take on VinFast and its 36% market share
news.summary: Tesla has begun hiring in Vietnam, signaling its official entry into the market, where VinFast dominates with a 36% share of new car sales.
news.body:
Tesla has started hiring in Vietnam, with roles including a sales manager, service manager, and a charging project developer. This marks the company's first confirmation of entering the Southeast Asian market, where local electric vehicle manufacturer VinFast holds a commanding 36% share of new car sales this year.

Tesla quietly registered Tesla Motors Vietnam LLC in Ho Chi Minh City on September 11, with a business scope covering car imports, wholesale, and retail. The company has not officially commented on the move, but internal recruitment efforts suggest a planned launch in the near future. The hiring of a charging project developer indicates Tesla's intention to establish a Supercharger network in the country.

Vietnam's market is currently dominated by VinFast, which has sold over 177,697 vehicles in the first nine months of 2026, outpacing its closest competitors combined. The company's success is partly due to its local manufacturing base in Haiphong and a growing charging network operated by its sister company, V-Green.

Despite these challenges, Tesla has a potential advantage: Vietnam has extended its registration fee exemption for battery-electric vehicles through 2030, which applies to both locally produced and imported EVs. This could help Tesla compete more effectively in the region.

Tesla's approach in Vietnam mirrors its strategy in other Southeast Asian markets, such as Thailand and the Philippines, where it launched after a period of hiring and market preparation. A Vietnam launch in the next few months would not be unexpected.

news.title: X Introduces Jarring Promotion Tool to Encourage Paid Posts
news.summary: X has introduced a new animated arm feature to draw attention to the 'promote' button, aiming to encourage users to pay for post promotion.
news.body:
X, formerly known as Twitter, has rolled out a new promotional feature designed to encourage users to pay for post promotion. The platform now displays an animated arm that reaches across the screen to highlight the 'promote' button while users are composing a post. This feature is part of X's broader strategy to increase revenue from paid promotions, following Elon Musk's recent warning that advertisers making 'ugly, shrill, strident, or overstate claims' about their products would be barred from advertising on the platform.

The animated arm has been described as unsettling by many users. Verified users and those with a paid X Premium subscription appear to be the only ones seeing the feature. Some users have shared images of the promotional tool, with reactions ranging from confusion to frustration. One user, Sheel Mohnot, stated, “I’ve never promoted a post and HATE this screen takeover.” Another, Jesse Middleton, compared the experience to a Halloween prank, calling the animation “truly shocking.”

The promote feature allows users to extend the reach of their posts to a larger audience based on location, interests, or demographics. Promoted posts are labeled as such, distinguishing them from regular content. This move aligns with X's ongoing efforts to monetize user-generated content and increase ad revenue, particularly under Musk's leadership. The feature is part of a larger trend of platforms pushing for more paid promotion options to sustain their business models.

While the feature is not available to all users, its introduction signals X's continued focus on driving engagement and monetization through paid promotions. The response from users has been mixed, with many expressing discomfort over the intrusive nature of the animated arm.

news.title: Tesla Semi catches fire on I-880 with no crash, closes freeway for 10 hours
news.summary: A Tesla Semi caught fire on I-880 in California without a crash, leading to a 10-hour freeway closure and raising safety concerns for the electric truck.
news.body:
A Tesla Semi caught fire on Interstate 880 in Hayward, California, on Tuesday evening, with no crash reported. The electric truck’s lithium-ion battery burned long enough to keep the southbound freeway closed for about 10 hours. The driver was unharmed, but the incident has raised questions about the safety of Tesla’s Semi trucks and their battery systems.

The fire broke out at around 5:35 p.m. PT in the southbound lanes near Route 92. The California Highway Patrol (CHP) closed I-880 in both directions due to the potential risk of hazardous chemical smoke. The driver told officers the truck caught fire and that they did not know why. No other vehicles were involved in the incident.

Northbound lanes reopened Tuesday night, while southbound lanes took longer to clear. CHP initially warned that the battery could burn for 15 to 18 hours, but crews managed to clear the road by around 3:30 a.m. Wednesday. Photos from the scene showed firefighters laying foam around the burned-out tractor, with the front of a Premier Trailer Leasing trailer charred behind it. The truck’s operator has not been identified, and Tesla has not commented on the incident.

This is the second time a Tesla Semi has caused a California interstate closure due to fire. In August 2024, a Tesla-operated Semi caught fire on I-80 near Emigrant Gap, and the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) later found the truck had left the road, hit a delineator post and a tree, and its battery ignited after the impact. This incident, however, occurred without a crash, shifting the focus to the truck’s internal systems.

Tesla only began volume production of the Semi in Nevada this year, after nearly a decade of delays. The company has secured significant orders, including 370 Semis from WattEV for use at the Port of Oakland. With a relatively small fleet in operation, one fire with no crash is a significant data point for Tesla and its customers.

The cause of the fire is under investigation. If the fire originated from a tire, brake, or trailer and spread to the tractor, it would be a regular trucking issue. However, if the battery pack experienced thermal runaway on its own, Tesla needs to determine the cause before tens of thousands of these trucks hit the road. The NTSB investigated the previous incident and should also look into this one. Tesla should publish its findings to address safety concerns and reassure customers.

news.title: Tesla's Emergency Drive Away feature used accidentally in Austin
news.summary: Tesla's Emergency Drive Away function was accidentally activated during a Supercharger session in Austin, causing damage to both the vehicle and the charging station.
news.body:
Tesla's 'Emergency Drive Away' function, designed to allow drivers to quickly leave a charging station in an emergency, was used for the first time in the real world — but not by choice. A Tesla owner in Austin accidentally triggered the feature while charging before heading to an F1 race. The feature unlatched the Supercharger connector, causing damage to both the vehicle and the charging station. The incident was captured on video and shared by a user on the r/TeslaLounge subreddit.

Tesla has warned that improper use of the Emergency Drive Away function could cost up to $25,000 in repairs. The company stated that drivers who activate the feature outside of an emergency situation would be responsible for all repair costs. According to Tesla, the feature should only be used in situations where there is an immediate threat to life or personal safety, or when exiting the vehicle is unsafe.

Following the incident, Tesla requires drivers who use the feature to schedule a service appointment to inspect and repair the vehicle. The feature is intended to provide a safe and quick way to leave a charging station in an emergency, but its accidental use highlights the importance of understanding how to use it properly.

The incident has sparked discussions among Tesla owners about the potential risks and costs associated with the feature. Tesla continues to emphasize that the Emergency Drive Away function is a safety tool meant for emergencies, not for routine use.

news.title: Tesla’s Cybercab battery design could make robotaxis even cheaper
news.summary: Tesla designed the Cybercab battery with extra space to potentially switch to LFP cells in the future, which could reduce costs and improve serviceability.
news.body:
Tesla’s Cybercab battery pack includes extra space designed to allow for a future switch to lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells, a move that could reduce costs and improve serviceability. According to Robert Sumpf, Tesla’s director of mechanical design engineering for battery modules and packs, the additional room was intentionally left to accommodate a transition to LFP chemistry as the company scales production. LFP cells, while less energy-dense than the current nickel-based 4680 cells, are cheaper, cooler, and more durable, making them an attractive option for robotaxis that require long-term reliability and cost efficiency.

The Cybercab’s battery design also diverges from Tesla’s earlier structural approach, which involved potting hundreds of cells into a single block. Instead, the Cybercab uses four separate, individually sealed modules. This modular design allows for easier repairs and replacements, reducing service costs. Sumpf criticized the older method, giving it a “grade D” due to its difficulty in manufacturing and near impossibility to repair. The new design aims to minimize the cost of replacing entire battery packs, which is a critical concern for a vehicle that is rarely parked and is expected to operate for hundreds of thousands of miles.

Tesla’s Cybercab is currently being produced at Giga Texas, with plans to deliver the first units to external customers by the end of 2026. However, the majority of the vehicles are expected to remain in Tesla’s Robotaxi fleet, operating as a transport service. While no timeline was provided for an LFP version of the battery, Tesla continues to expand its Robotaxi fleet, with over 500 Cybercabs authorized for use in the fleet as of recent records.

The design choices reflect Tesla’s focus on long-term cost efficiency and serviceability, which are crucial for the success of its robotaxi business model.

news.title: Louisiana residents sue to unwind SpaceX tax deal
news.summary: Louisiana residents have filed a lawsuit seeking to overturn a tax agreement with SpaceX, citing concerns over public benefits and transparency.
news.body: Residents of Louisiana have initiated legal action to challenge a tax deal involving SpaceX, arguing that the agreement does not provide sufficient public benefits or transparency. The lawsuit claims that the terms of the deal, which granted SpaceX tax incentives, were not properly disclosed to the public or adequately scrutinized by local authorities. The residents are seeking to have the agreement invalidated or revised to ensure that the benefits to the community are more clearly defined and equitable. The case has drawn attention from local officials and community members who are concerned about the impact of such agreements on public resources and accountability. SpaceX has not yet commented on the lawsuit, but the company has previously emphasized its commitment to supporting local communities through job creation and infrastructure development. The legal battle could set a precedent for how similar tax incentives are reviewed and approved in the future. The lawsuit highlights ongoing debates about corporate tax agreements and their implications for public policy and community interests. If successful, the case may lead to changes in how such deals are negotiated and implemented, potentially affecting other companies seeking similar incentives. The outcome of the lawsuit remains uncertain as it moves through the legal system.

news.title: Musk's Tesla Incentive Plan Details Revealed
news.summary: Elon Musk's long-term performance incentive plan at Tesla includes 423.7 million shares, contingent on market and operational milestones.
news.body: Elon Musk's compensation structure at Tesla Inc. includes a long-term performance incentive plan that could reward him with up to 423.7 million shares of Tesla stock, representing about 12% of the company. The shares are distributed in 12 tranches, each tied to specific market and operational milestones. The market capitalization milestones range from $2 trillion to $8.5 trillion, while the operational milestones include eight annual earnings targets and four product delivery goals. These include delivering 20 million Tesla vehicles, achieving 10 million active FSD subscriptions, delivering 1 million bots, and having 1 million robotaxis in commercial operation. If Musk meets all the criteria by 2030, the shares will vest in March 2033. If not, they will vest in September 2035. Should he leave Tesla before any shares vest, he will forfeit them. The potential value of the award, if all milestones are met at an $8.5 trillion market cap, could exceed $1 trillion. The plan outlines the conditions under which Musk would receive these shares, emphasizing Tesla's long-term growth and operational achievements. The agreement highlights the company's ambitious goals and Musk's alignment with its future success. The performance-based structure aims to incentivize Musk to drive Tesla toward significant financial and operational milestones over the next decade.

news.title: Korean police book 80 Tesla drivers over illegal FSD unlock devices
news.summary: Seoul police have arrested 80 individuals for using unauthorized devices to activate Tesla's Full Self-Driving feature in vehicles not approved for it in South Korea.
news.body:
Seoul police have booked 80 people for using aftermarket devices to enable Tesla’s Full Self-Driving (FSD) feature in cars that are not legally allowed to run it in South Korea. Authorities also seized 21 of these devices. This is the largest enforcement action to date against FSD 'jailbreak' hardware, which has been circulating in China, Europe, and Korea over the past year.

The suspects either imported the unlock modules from Europe and China or built their own. One individual used a European-made unit, while another, an IT worker, constructed his device using information from GitHub. Suspects also shared online advice on how to unlock FSD and how to prevent the car from recording its activation.

They are being charged under Korea’s Motor Vehicle Management Act, which prohibits unauthorized software changes that could affect vehicle safety. The penalty includes up to two years in prison or a fine of up to 20 million won (about $15,000). The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport requested the investigation in April after detecting signs of unauthorized FSD activation. Authorities are consulting with the Korea Transportation Safety Authority on the technical aspects of the case.

Most Korean Teslas cannot legally use FSD. Tesla introduced FSD (Supervised) in South Korea in late 2025, but only on US-built vehicles like the Model S, Model X, and Cybertruck. These models are exempt from Korean safety certification due to the Korea-US free trade agreement. However, the Model 3 and Model Y, which are produced in Shanghai, have not met Korea’s safety standards for FSD. As of August, only about 20.7% of the 229,311 Teslas on Korean roads can legally use FSD.

Tesla has taken steps to combat these devices, including remotely detecting them and removing FSD from affected cars. It has also warned owners of potential liability for crashes and loss of warranty coverage. Some Chinese owners have been permanently banned from FSD.

The situation highlights a growing issue where Tesla sells features that cannot be legally used in certain regions, creating a market for unauthorized modifications. Now that Korean authorities are taking legal action, questions remain about whether Tesla will refund owners who purchased FSD for vehicles that may never be allowed to use it.

news.title: United CEO calls Starlink 'biggest competitive advantage' but says it's temporary
news.summary: United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby described Starlink as the airline's leading competitive advantage, but warned that the edge is temporary as other carriers catch up.
news.body:
United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby has called SpaceX’s Starlink satellite internet the airline’s biggest competitive advantage in the U.S. market. However, he acknowledged that this advantage is temporary, as all major airlines are expected to adopt similar technology in the coming years. Kirby emphasized that United aims to capitalize on its current head start by converting trial users into long-term loyal customers.

United has been moving faster than its competitors in deploying Starlink. As of mid-to-late October 2026, the system was installed on roughly 43 percent of its fleet, with plans to reach 61 percent by year-end and full coverage by the end of 2027. The airline already operates more Starlink-equipped flights than the rest of the U.S. industry combined.

Los Angeles International Airport is set to become United’s first 100 percent Starlink hub in the first half of 2027. The United app will also display the likelihood that any given flight has Starlink service. Kirby noted that early evidence suggests the offering influences booking decisions, with some passengers switching flights for Starlink connectivity.

Competitors are moving more slowly. Southwest Airlines began installations in 2025 and expects to complete them soon. Delta is pursuing Amazon’s Leo system, while American Airlines plans to start Starlink work in early 2027. This timeline gap gives United a multi-year window in which it remains the only major U.S. carrier offering Starlink at scale.

Kirby has framed the strategy as pressing the advantage while simultaneously widening gaps in other technology areas. The approach reflects a calculated bet that superior in-flight connectivity can accelerate share gains and support longer-term financial targets, including a 10 percent pre-tax margin goal.

news.title: Tesla Cybercab’s unorthodox paint process explained
news.summary: Tesla’s Cybercab skips traditional paint shops, using material science and in-mold coloring to reduce costs and factory space.
news.body:
Tesla’s Cybercab production at Giga Texas eliminates the traditional paint shop, a major cost and space-saving move. This decision was based on the use of specialized alloys that do not oxidize or lose strength over time, reducing the need for conventional painting. Tesla Vice President of Vehicle Engineering Lars Moravy explained that the company’s core rule is to question requirements, including the need for paint.

Conventional paint lines are expensive and space-consuming, requiring hundreds of millions of dollars and a million man-hours to build. By avoiding this step, Tesla cuts factory floor space per car by about 50%. The Cybercab’s front and rear castings are made from aluminum alloys that do not oxidize, while only the side modules receive an anti-corrosion dip coat.

Exterior colors are integrated into the manufacturing process through reaction injection molding (RIM). Color is mixed into a polyurethane resin at the mix head before injection, resulting in colored body panels with a Class-A surface. This process avoids defects like orange peel and paint bleed, and shallow scratches can be repaired with compatible coatings.

The paint strategy is less about aesthetics and more about eliminating capital-intensive steps. Tesla has also explored in-mold lamination and painted films on stamped panels. The modular production process, combined with the absence of a paint shop, significantly reduces factory space and environmental impact.

This approach exemplifies Tesla’s application of first-principles thinking to streamline manufacturing and reduce costs.

news.title: Musk claims Tesla Robotaxi win over Waymo, but data shows Waymo leads by 7x
news.summary: Elon Musk claims Tesla's Robotaxi has surpassed Waymo in Austin, but national data shows Waymo still leads by a significant margin.
news.body:
Elon Musk has claimed that Tesla's Robotaxi has won the race against Waymo in Austin, citing a single week of driverless miles. Tesla reported 438,000 miles in the week ending October 18, surpassing Waymo's 406,000 weekly average in the city. However, this figure is based on data that is four months old for Waymo, as the company publishes its safety data with a delay.

The comparison is further complicated by the fact that Tesla's figure represents its best week ever, while Waymo's data is an average from the second quarter of 2026. Nationally, Waymo still leads by a wide margin. In Q2 2026, Waymo averaged 3.90 million rider-only miles per week, compared to Tesla's 558,000 miles in its best week. Waymo's Phoenix, Bay Area, and Los Angeles markets each drive more miles per week than Tesla's entire network.

Tesla's surge in Austin is attributed to the launch of public Cybercab rides in September. The company has registered 463 Cybercabs in Texas, with 337 added in the last 30 days. Tesla's strategy involves deploying a large number of vehicles in a single city to boost mileage, which may not be replicable elsewhere.

Despite the growth in Austin, Tesla's driverless miles are still limited by software constraints. Tesla's AI software head, Ashok Elluswamy, noted that the service is constrained by the software, not by regulators. Tesla's vehicles avoid highways and at-grade railroad crossings, which can lead to longer trip times and increased mileage.

Waymo, on the other hand, has been operating on freeways in Phoenix, San Francisco, and Los Angeles since November 2025. This highlights a significant difference in the level of autonomy between the two companies, with Waymo currently leading in terms of operational scope and scale.

news.title: SpaceX launches Starlink satellites from California in early morning mission
news.summary: SpaceX successfully launched 27 Starlink satellites from California in an early morning mission, marking the 117th Falcon 9 launch of 2026.
news.body:
SpaceX conducted a successful Falcon 9 launch from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California on October 27, delivering 27 Starlink satellites to low Earth orbit. The launch took place at 3:25 a.m. EDT, targeting night owls rather than early risers.

The Falcon 9 rocket's first stage, B1082, separated approximately 2.5 minutes into the flight and landed on the droneship Of Course I Still Love You (OCISLY) in the Pacific Ocean. This marked B1082's 21st Starlink mission and its 26th overall flight, which includes previous missions such as USSF-62 and Transporter-18.

The upper stage of the Falcon 9 ignited its engine for a second time about 53 minutes after liftoff, circularizing the orbit before deploying the Starlink satellites. The mission was the 117th Falcon 9 launch of 2026, with about three-quarters of those launches dedicated to Starlink.

As SpaceX continues to develop its Starship rocket, the company has begun shifting focus away from Falcon 9. This includes ending Starlink launches from Florida earlier this year. Despite this, the Falcon 9 remains a key asset in expanding the Starlink network, which now includes over 11,000 active satellites.

news.title: Tesla's Cybercab Production Outpaces Deployment
news.summary: Tesla's Cybercab production line is now faster than its deployment capabilities, according to Vice President of Vehicle Engineering Lars Moravy.
news.body:
Tesla’s Cybercab production line in Texas is currently building robotaxis faster than the company can deploy them, according to Lars Moravy, Tesla’s Vice President of Vehicle Engineering. Moravy noted in a recent deep dive from Munro Live that the manufacturing line is outpacing deployment efforts, creating a bottleneck on the operational side. The Cybercab line is capable of producing over 125,000 units annually, with the potential to exceed that capacity, according to Moravy’s comments.

The production process for the Cybercab is highly automated, with the vehicle split into front, rear, side, and center modules that are built and tested separately before being assembled on a short final line. This final line contains only 25 fully automated stations, significantly fewer than what is required for a Model Y. The full line is about 78% automated, with the framing line already at 100% automation. The design also uses roughly 50% less floor space per vehicle compared to traditional models.

Tesla has also made significant changes to the Cybercab’s design to enhance durability and efficiency. The vehicle is engineered to last at least 500,000 miles, which is crucial for a robotaxi that will be in constant use. The battery system features an 88S6P pack of 4680 cells in a steel enclosure, with each module potted separately to allow for individual module replacement. Wireless battery management boards and fast contactors eliminate the need for a pyro fuse, improving reliability and safety.

Despite the impressive production capabilities, the deployment of Cybercabs remains a challenge. Tesla has already deployed over 50 units for the Formula 1 weekend in Austin, with 463 Cybercabs registered in Texas. The company aims to launch Cybercab service in Dallas next month and expects to deliver units to customers by the end of 2026. However, as of now, no Cybercabs are available for purchase by the public.

news.title: Tesla may resume selling US-built Model 3s in Canada amid quota issues
news.summary: Tesla Canada has updated its website with specs matching the Fremont-built Model 3, suggesting a possible return of US-made vehicles before Shanghai-built models resume.
news.body:
Tesla Canada has updated the specifications for the Model 3 Premium Rear-Wheel Drive on its website, showing a range of 584 km and a 0-100 km/h time of 5.2 seconds. These numbers align with the Fremont-built Long Range RWD model that Tesla previously sold in Canada, rather than the Shanghai-built version currently listed at 463 km and 6.2 seconds.

The change was first noticed by a Canadian Tesla owner on X, who pointed out the new figures in the 'Model 3 Premium Specs' section. The updated page now includes a curb weight of 1,745 kg and promises 'up to 584 km (EPA est.) on a single charge.' However, Tesla's Canadian comparison page still lists the older specs, indicating a potential discrepancy or delay in updates.

The Fremont-built Model 3 Long Range RWD was previously available in Canada at a starting price of $54,990 and was eligible for the federal iZEV rebate. This model matches the current US-sold Premium RWD, which has a 363-mile EPA range (equivalent to 584 km) and a 0-60 mph time of 4.9 seconds. The Shanghai-built version, while offering a longer range of 830 km, is currently unavailable due to quota restrictions.

Tesla faces challenges with Canada's 25% counter-tariffs on US-made vehicles, which were implemented in April 2025. These tariffs significantly increased the cost of US-built models, leading Tesla to discontinue them in Canada earlier this year. If Tesla were to reintroduce the Fremont-built Model 3, it would likely be priced around $65,000 to $67,000, exceeding the $50,000 limit of Canada's new EV Affordability Program.

Currently, the only Model 3 available for order in Canada is the Performance variant, priced at $74,990. Analysts suggest that Tesla may be preparing a temporary solution by reintroducing the Fremont-built Premium RWD to fill the gap until Shanghai-built models become available in March 2027.

news.title: Falcon 9 and GSLV Rockets Set for Upcoming Launches
news.summary: Falcon 9 and GSLV rockets are scheduled for launches, marking significant developments in space exploration.
news.body: Falcon 9 and GSLV rockets are set to launch in the near future, highlighting ongoing efforts in space exploration. The Falcon 9, developed by SpaceX, is known for its reusability and cost-effectiveness in delivering payloads to orbit. Meanwhile, the GSLV, developed by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), is a key player in India's space program. These launches are expected to contribute to various scientific and commercial missions. The Falcon 9 has been instrumental in supporting satellite deployments and crewed missions to the International Space Station. The GSLV is anticipated to carry payloads that support national and international research initiatives. Both launches underscore the collaborative and competitive nature of the global space industry. SpaceX continues to push the boundaries of space technology with its Falcon 9, while ISRO remains a significant force in the region. The upcoming launches are part of a broader trend of increased activity in space exploration and commercial satellite deployment. These events are closely watched by industry experts and space enthusiasts alike. The success of these launches will have implications for future missions and technological advancements in the sector. As the countdown begins, anticipation builds for what these launches will achieve in the realm of space exploration.

news.title: SpaceX secures $40B debt financing for AI infrastructure
news.summary: SpaceX has closed a $40 billion debt financing deal to support its AI infrastructure needs, as the company continues to expand its capabilities beyond rockets and satellites.
news.body: SpaceX has secured a $40 billion debt financing deal to fund its growing AI infrastructure operations. The move comes as the company continues to invest heavily in artificial intelligence, leveraging its vast computational resources for various applications. Elon Musk confirmed the deal on X, highlighting the challenges faced by companies reliant on AI data centers in accessing capital. He noted that debt markets have largely shut off access to money for companies without substantial revenue independent of AI data centers, leading to a wave of consolidation among smaller players in the space. This development underscores the increasing importance of AI infrastructure in SpaceX's broader operations, which now include significant investments in computing power and data processing capabilities. The financing will support SpaceX's ongoing efforts to build and maintain the computational resources necessary for its AI initiatives, which are expected to play a crucial role in the company's future projects. As the AI funding landscape becomes more competitive, SpaceX's ability to secure such a large financing deal positions it as a major player in the rapidly evolving AI industry. The move also reflects the growing recognition of the strategic value of AI infrastructure in the broader tech ecosystem, with companies like SpaceX leading the charge in this new frontier. With the AI funding window closing, securing capital has become a critical factor for companies aiming to stay ahead in the race for technological innovation. SpaceX's recent financing deal is a clear indication of its commitment to maintaining a strong position in this increasingly competitive landscape.

news.title: SpaceX Raptor 4 Engine to Deliver 300 Ton Thrust at Same Mass as Raptor 3
news.summary: SpaceX is set to significantly boost the thrust of its Raptor engine while maintaining its mass, enhancing the performance of the Super Heavy booster.
news.body:
SpaceX has been steadily improving the Raptor engine family, increasing sea-level thrust while reducing mass. This iterative engineering has led to a substantial performance boost for the Super Heavy booster. Elon Musk recently shared details on the upcoming Raptor 4, which is expected to deliver 300 metric tons of thrust at roughly the same mass as Raptor 3.

Raptor 1 initially provided 185 metric tons of thrust at 2,080 kilograms. Raptor 2 improved this to 230 tons at 1,630 kilograms. Raptor 3 targets 280 tons at 1,525 kilograms, with operational ratings near 250 tons. Raptor 4 will push this further to 300 tons, marking a more than 60 percent increase in thrust from the first iteration.

With 33 engines on the Super Heavy booster, the jump to Raptor 4 would result in approximately 9,900 metric tons of total liftoff thrust. This is nearly three times the thrust of the Saturn V rocket, which had five F-1 engines producing about 3,400 metric tons of thrust.

Higher sea-level thrust improves the initial thrust-to-weight ratio of the full stack, leading to faster acceleration off the pad. This reduces the time spent fighting gravity, which is a major drain on total available delta-v. Every second shaved off during the early climb preserves more propellant energy for reaching orbital velocity or carrying extra payload.

Maintaining the same mass for Raptor 4 while increasing thrust improves the engine's own thrust-to-weight ratio and reduces the structural and propellant mass fraction needed to support the engines. These improvements allow for greater propellant capacity, larger payloads, and higher flight rates, which are essential for large-scale space transport.

The practical effects of these advancements are significant for Starship's architecture. Greater liftoff thrust supports heavier vehicles, larger propellant loads, and higher payloads to low Earth orbit, which SpaceX has targeted in the 100-plus-ton reusable range. This capacity underpins orbital refueling, lunar missions, and eventual Mars cargo and crew flights.

news.title: Tesla Cybertruck Stopped in Germany Over Legal Restrictions
news.summary: A Tesla Cybertruck was stopped in Germany due to legal restrictions, highlighting the vehicle's incompatibility with European road regulations.
news.body:
A Tesla Cybertruck was pulled over in Germany, illustrating the challenges of operating the vehicle on European roads. The Cybertruck's design has raised concerns among regulators, particularly regarding pedestrian protection standards. As a result, the vehicle lacks 'type approval' in Germany, making it illegal for regular use on the country's roads.

The Cybertruck's size also poses a problem. While it weighs less than 3,500kg, the 'Gross Vehicle Weight' of the vehicle exceeds this limit when fully loaded. This means that drivers typically holding a 'class B' license, which allows operation of vehicles up to 3,500kg, are not legally permitted to drive the Cybertruck. Instead, a 'C1' license, which permits vehicles up to 7.5 tons, is required.

A Swedish driver was stopped near Vaterstatten, close to the southern border of Germany, for driving the Cybertruck without the appropriate license. The police denied the driver the right to continue, citing the need for a higher-class license. The driver had reportedly registered the vehicle in Poland but still faced legal issues due to the lack of proper licensing and speed restrictions.

German regulations also require vehicles registered in the country to be limited to a maximum speed of 90 km/h (56 mph). The Cybertruck in question did not meet this requirement, further complicating its legal status. The incident underscores the difficulties of operating the Cybertruck in Europe, where individual exemptions are rare and often denied.

Despite these restrictions, some drivers have managed to operate the Cybertruck in Europe by securing individual approvals from specific countries. However, this incident highlights the potential legal risks associated with driving an unapproved vehicle on European roads.

news.title: Elon Musk warns of 'guppy-level death' for 200+ neoclouds
news.summary: Elon Musk warned that over 200 neocloud companies could collapse due to financial strain, citing a lack of access to capital for those without substantial revenue.
news.body:
Elon Musk, CEO of SpaceX and Tesla, warned that more than 200 neocloud companies could face significant financial challenges, leading to what he described as 'guppy-level death' and consolidation in the sector. His comments came amid growing concerns about debt-fueled expansion and the ability of AI infrastructure companies to generate returns.

Musk noted that debt markets have largely closed off access to capital for companies that do not have substantial revenue independent of AI data centers. He suggested that many neoclouds would struggle to survive, with only a few expected to make it through the current economic climate. SpaceX, which operates its own data centers, is a direct competitor to these companies, which also provide computing resources for AI development.

The warning follows a post by Chamath Palihapitiya, founder of Social Capital, who predicted that 2027 would be a turbulent year for the sector, with many companies facing financial difficulties. Neocloud stocks have already taken a hit, with companies like CoreWeave, Nebius, and Iren experiencing significant declines in value.

Nvidia, a major investor in several neoclouds, has expressed confidence in the demand for AI infrastructure, though it acknowledged a shortage of capital to support the sector's growth. Executives from Nebius and Iren have also defended their companies, stating that customer demand remains strong and that they are not facing the same level of debt as some of their peers.

The situation highlights the growing risks in the AI infrastructure space, as companies race to build out data centers while navigating a challenging financial landscape.

news.title: Tesla partners with Turo to offer FSD test drives for renters
news.summary: Tesla has partnered with car rental platform Turo to allow renters to access vehicles with Full Self-Driving (Supervised) enabled, aiming to boost FSD adoption and subscriptions.
news.body:
Tesla has partnered with Turo to allow US renters to access vehicles with Full Self-Driving (Supervised) enabled, marking a new approach to testing and promoting its advanced driver assistance system. The feature will launch on October 28, allowing users to filter for FSD-enabled Teslas through a direct integration with Tesla's API. This move provides a broader audience with the opportunity to experience FSD, which Tesla has been pushing as a subscription-based service since February 2024.

Turo hosts can link their Tesla accounts to the platform, which verifies each car's FSD status. Eligible hosts can also receive a free one-month FSD trial, after which the standard $99 monthly subscription applies. Turo claims thousands of FSD-enabled Teslas are already listed, with the Model 3 and Model Y being among the most popular vehicles on the platform.

The partnership is part of Tesla's broader strategy to increase FSD adoption, especially as it tracks toward a milestone of 10 million active subscriptions. The company has been offering free FSD trials with new Model 3 and Model Y purchases, and this new initiative could help convert renters into long-term subscribers.

However, the integration raises concerns about user understanding and safety. FSD (Supervised) is a level 2 driver assistance system, and the driver remains fully responsible at all times. Turo encourages renters to review Tesla's safety guidelines before using the feature, but it has not clarified liability in the event of an accident involving FSD.

The partnership with Turo represents a step toward Tesla's long-term vision of a 'Tesla Network,' where owners can rent out their vehicles for rides. While the current arrangement is limited to Turo, it provides Tesla with a new avenue to showcase FSD and potentially increase its user base.

Despite the potential benefits, the rollout highlights the ongoing challenge of ensuring user awareness and responsible use of FSD technology. As Tesla continues to push the boundaries of autonomous driving, the balance between innovation and safety remains a critical concern.

news.title: Starship Flight 15 booster completes full 33-engine static fire
news.summary: Super Heavy Booster 22 fired all 33 Raptor 3 engines at Starbase on October 25, a key step before Starship Flight 15.
news.body:
SpaceX lit all 33 Raptor 3 engines on Super Heavy Booster 22 for roughly 15 seconds at Starbase in South Texas on Sunday, October 25. The company described it on X as a full-duration static fire for the booster assigned to Flight 15.

The test kicks off the final round of checks on the first stage. Booster 22 will later be stacked with Ship 42, the upper stage for the mission, but the ship still has to complete its own static fire and final systems checks before the pair can fly.

## An ambitious flight

Flight 15 is shaping up to be one of the most demanding Starship missions yet. Elon Musk has said SpaceX will try to catch the ship upper stage with the launch tower for the first time, in addition to catching the booster. Catching both stages is central to SpaceX's plan to make Starship fully and rapidly reusable.

The mission follows Flight 14 in late September, the first Starship flight to reach orbit and the first to carry working payloads, a batch of Starlink V3 satellites. Recent FAA planning material lists early-to-mid November as the tentative window for Flight 15, though dates for a development programme like this often slip.

news.title: Tesla Assisted Driving expands to tenth EU country
news.summary: Tesla has expanded its Tesla Assisted Driving (TAD) to Latvia, marking the tenth EU country to approve the system.
news.body:
Tesla has expanded its Tesla Assisted Driving (TAD) suite to Latvia, the tenth European Union country to approve the company’s advanced driver assistance technology. The approval follows a provisional European type approval granted by the Netherlands’ RDW authority on April 10, 2026. Latvia’s Road Traffic Safety Directorate (CSDD) evaluated the Dutch documentation, coordinated with other national authorities, and reviewed updates from Tesla, including tightened speed offset limits and stronger driver monitoring.

In Europe, the feature is now marketed as Tesla Assisted Driving after a recent rule change deemed the name 'Full Self-Driving' misleading. The system remains an SAE Level 2 driver assistance tool, capable of controlling speed, steering, braking, lane changes, and intersections while following a navigation route. Drivers must continuously monitor the road and be prepared to intervene immediately.

The sequence of EU recognitions began with the Netherlands in April and continued through Lithuania, Estonia, Denmark, Belgium, Slovenia, Czechia, Croatia, and Slovakia. Most countries have relied on mutual recognition of the Dutch provisional approval rather than independent national testing. However, an EU-wide decision requires a qualified majority in the Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles, with larger markets like Germany, France, and Italy still under review. A vote is expected this December.

For Latvian Tesla owners with compatible vehicles and software, the imminent rollout expands access to the supervised system while emphasizing the need for attentive human oversight.

news.title: Astranis Upgrades Falcon 9 Contract for Dedicated Satellite Launch
news.summary: Astranis has upgraded its Falcon 9 launch contract with SpaceX to a dedicated mission for its entire Block 4 satellite production run, set for 2028.
news.body:
Astranis has announced an upgrade to its existing launch contract with SpaceX, transitioning the fourth launch to a dedicated mission for its entire Block 4 production run of MicroGEO satellites. The mission, scheduled for 2028, will carry six MicroGEO satellites directly into geostationary orbit (GEO) using an Impulse Helios upper stage. This marks a significant step in Astranis’ expansion of high-orbit infrastructure and will increase its total fleet size to 16 satellites.

The upgraded contract allows Astranis to fully utilize the payload capacity of the Falcon 9 rocket for this mission. This follows an initial agreement signed with SpaceX in late 2024. The move supports Astranis’ responsive business model, which focuses on securing dedicated launches for multi-satellite blocks to meet growing demand for controlled space infrastructure.

Governments and enterprises are increasingly seeking dedicated space infrastructure for communications and other missions, such as space domain awareness. Higher orbits like GEO are uniquely suited for these requirements. John Gedmark, CEO and co-founder of Astranis, noted that the company is ramping up production to meet demand for commercial and national security missions.

This contract follows the recent introduction of Perceptor, a system that extends Astranis’ capabilities beyond communications into space domain awareness and maneuverability. The company has already secured a backlog of over $1 billion in commercial contracts and is expanding its high-orbit platforms to connect, safeguard, and sustain critical infrastructure in GEO.

Astranis, based in Northern California, has raised over $1.2 billion from top investors and employs more than 500 engineers and entrepreneurs. The company designs, builds, and operates its satellites from its 153,000 sq. ft. headquarters.

news.title: Tesla Cybercabs dominate Austin F1 weekend with record sightings
news.summary: Tesla's Cybercabs made a major appearance during the Austin F1 Grand Prix, setting a new record for sightings and showcasing the company's progress in autonomous vehicle deployment.
news.body:
Tesla's Cybercabs were in full force during the Austin F1 Grand Prix, marking one of the largest public deployments of the autonomous vehicle fleet to date. The event served as a major stress test for the robotaxis, with sightings reaching a record high. Tesla's head of AI software, Ashok Elluswamy, shared a photo of a long line of gold Cybercabs and Model Y Robotaxis near the Circuit of the Americas, highlighting the scale of the operation. The fleet was also used to transport fans back to their homes after the race, with ride requests continuing well into the night.

The deployment was carefully planned in advance, with the Robotaxi app showing expanded service areas around the track. However, not all areas were accessible, and some riders found the drop-off points inconvenient. Cybercab Spotter, a tracking account, reported 1,250 sightings in Austin on Saturday, surpassing the previous record. This number reflects the fleet's activity rather than its total size, as the Texas automated vehicle registry listed 463 Cybercabs registered in the area.

Tesla has not yet disclosed the number of rides provided during the event or whether the expanded service area and late-night cutoff will remain after the race weekend. The company has previously indicated plans to extend service hours and operate Robotaxi around the clock by the end of the year. Additionally, Tesla aims to deliver the first Cybercabs to external customers before the end of 2026, marking a significant shift in the vehicle's deployment strategy.

## Battery Design for Future Cost Reduction
Tesla's Cybercab battery design includes extra space for a potential switch to lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells, which could reduce costs and improve serviceability. The design allows for future upgrades without compromising range, and the modular battery structure enables easier repairs and replacements. This innovation is expected to play a key role in making robotaxis more affordable and sustainable in the long term.

news.title: Possible Roberts Road Expansion as SpaceX pushes for Flight 16
news.summary: SpaceX is considering expanding Roberts Road to accommodate increased traffic related to its upcoming Flight 16 launch.
news.body: SpaceX is evaluating the possibility of expanding Roberts Road near its launch site to manage the anticipated rise in traffic associated with Flight 16. The expansion would help ensure smoother operations and reduce delays during the busy launch period. The company has not yet confirmed the details of the project, but officials have indicated that infrastructure improvements are a priority as launch schedules become more frequent. This potential development comes as SpaceX continues to increase its operational pace, with multiple launches planned in the coming months. Local authorities are being consulted to assess the feasibility of the expansion and its impact on surrounding areas. The project is part of broader efforts to support SpaceX's growing operations and maintain efficiency at the launch site. If approved, the expansion could be completed in time for Flight 16, which is expected to take place in the near future. SpaceX has a history of working closely with local governments to address infrastructure needs related to its missions. This initiative highlights the company's commitment to ensuring that its operations do not disrupt the surrounding community while meeting the demands of an increasingly active launch schedule. The expansion would also align with SpaceX's long-term goals of increasing the frequency of launches and reducing costs through operational efficiencies. As the company prepares for Flight 16, the focus remains on ensuring that all aspects of the mission, including infrastructure, are properly managed to support continued success.

news.title: Tesla Cybercab Adds Rear Camera and Quiet Mode Features
news.summary: Tesla has introduced rear camera and quiet mode features to its Cybercab, enhancing passenger experience and usability.
news.body:
Tesla has rolled out new features for its Cybercab, allowing passengers to view a live rear camera feed and activate a quiet mode to darken the cabin screen. These updates were discovered by riders in Austin, who shared their experiences on social media. The rear camera view provides passengers with visibility of what is behind the vehicle, addressing a design limitation of the Cybercab, which lacks traditional mirrors and a rear window.

The quiet mode feature, which darkens the screen, was also noted by riders. This addition aims to improve passenger comfort, particularly during nighttime rides or when passengers wish to rest. The features were implemented quickly following a request from a Cybercab rider, indicating Tesla's responsiveness to user feedback.

The introduction of these features highlights Tesla's ongoing efforts to refine the Cybercab experience. The company is also preparing the Cybercab for broader deployment outside its own fleet, with plans to deliver the vehicles to customers by the end of 2026. However, it remains unclear if these features will be extended to Tesla's Model Y Robotaxi fleet.

The updates come as part of a series of improvements for Cybercab riders in Austin, including a redesigned Live Activity for iPhone and Apple Watch and live trip sharing. These enhancements reflect Tesla's commitment to continuously improving its autonomous vehicle offerings.

news.title: SpaceX launches Starlink satellites from California as Falcon 9 cadence slows
news.summary: SpaceX launched a new batch of Starlink satellites from California, marking a shift in focus toward its Starship rocket.
news.body:
SpaceX launched its newest batch of Starlink broadband internet satellites from the California coast on October 23. The Falcon 9 rocket carried 27 satellites into low Earth orbit, continuing the expansion of the Starlink constellation. This mission marked the 116th Falcon 9 flight of 2026, with the majority of these launches dedicated to Starlink missions.

The Falcon 9's first stage booster, B1063, successfully landed on SpaceX's droneship 'Of Course I Still Love You' after separating from the second stage. This was B1063's 36th launch and landing, including its role in NASA's DART asteroid mission in 2021. The second stage will perform a second burn to place the satellites into their intended orbit, with deployment expected about 62 minutes after launch.

SpaceX is gradually shifting its focus from the Falcon 9 to its larger Starship rocket, which is designed for full reusability and can carry the upgraded Version 3 Starlink satellites. Once Starship becomes operational, the Falcon 9 and its Falcon Heavy variant are expected to be phased out. This transition has led to a slower Starlink launch cadence, with missions now occurring less frequently than in previous years.

The reduced frequency of Falcon 9 launches has already made 2025 the busiest year for the rocket, with 165 launches completed. At the current rate, the Falcon 9 is expected to complete just under 150 missions by the end of 2026.

news.title: Tesla cancels Cybertruck in Australia and NZ after 7 years of deposits
news.summary: Tesla has officially cancelled the Cybertruck for Australia and New Zealand, refunding deposits and offering FSD subscriptions to affected customers.
news.body:
Tesla has officially cancelled the Cybertruck for Australia and New Zealand. Reservation holders are receiving emails informing them that their orders are void and deposits will be refunded. Australians began reserving the electric pickup in November 2019, waiting nearly seven years for a vehicle Tesla now says it will not produce for the region.

The company stated in the email that plans to produce the Cybertruck for these markets have been discontinued. As a result, reservations cannot be fulfilled, and refunds will be processed within 30 days. Tesla is offering a free one-year subscription to FSD (Supervised) to reservation holders who switch to a new Model 3 or Model Y.

The decision comes after Tesla quietly closed the Australian reservation page in 2022 and replaced it with a “Get updates” button. No refunds were issued at the time, and customers continued waiting. In 2024, Tesla sent a Cybertruck to Australia for a display tour, but no right-hand-drive version was ever produced.

The core issue is that the Cybertruck is built only in left-hand drive, which is not suitable for countries like Australia and New Zealand. Certification and adaptation for these markets would be costly, and demand for the vehicle has not been strong enough to justify such an investment.

Tesla’s international Cybertruck launches have been limited to left-hand-drive markets, with deliveries beginning in South Korea and the UAE. The vehicle remains blocked in the EU due to pedestrian safety concerns. Sales of the Cybertruck have also declined in the US, raising questions about its long-term viability.

This decision highlights the challenges Tesla faces with the Cybertruck, which is now primarily a niche product in the US. The company is focusing on selling existing left-hand-drive units in international markets rather than investing in new production lines.

news.title: Tesla's $10B Texas solar factory could get 35 years of tax breaks
news.summary: Tesla's proposed $10 billion solar factory in Texas could receive up to 35 years of tax breaks, according to agreements approved by Fort Bend County commissioners.
news.body:
Tesla’s proposed $10 billion solar factory in Texas, known as Project Crystal Sun, could receive up to 35 years of tax breaks, according to agreements approved by Fort Bend County commissioners. The vote was unanimous, though Tesla has not yet committed to building the plant in Texas.

The tax incentives include a 10-year property tax abatement on equipment and inventory, followed by a 20-year grant covering 90% of county taxes on the same assets. If Tesla meets specific employment targets, the agreement could extend to 35 years. The plant, if built, would be located near Richmond, southwest of Houston, and is expected to begin commercial production by Q1 2029.

The agreements cover different aspects of Tesla’s tax obligations. The Chapter 312 tax abatement covers equipment and inventory for 10 years, while the Chapter 381 incentive agreement provides a 90% tax rebate for the next 20 years. A foreign trade zone agreement would exempt inventory from local property tax in exchange for Tesla making payments in lieu of taxes (PILOT).

To qualify for the tax breaks, Tesla must meet specific employment and investment targets. It must start construction by June 30, 2027, and invest $10 billion by December 31, 2031. If Tesla averages at least 12,000 employees for two consecutive years during the first decade, the tax rebate period could extend to 25 years.

The county’s minimum guarantee is $2 million annually, and Tesla’s own consultant estimated the project would generate $276.5 million in general taxes over 38 years without incentives. However, Tesla has not yet confirmed its commitment to build the plant in Texas, and the state still needs to approve the school-tax portion of the agreement.

The deal highlights the competitive nature of site selection for large-scale manufacturing projects. Fort Bend County’s economic development director stated the county would have been eliminated from consideration without these agreements. The outcome remains uncertain as Tesla has not officially committed to the project.

news.title: SpaceX books $561 million gain on its Boring Company stake
news.summary: SpaceX's quarterly filing shows a $561 million unrealised gain from its stake in The Boring Company, which recently raised $3 billion at a $23 billion valuation.
news.body:
SpaceX recorded an unrealised investment gain of $561 million in the third quarter from its stake in The Boring Company, according to its quarterly filing with the SEC. The gain made up more than half of SpaceX's other income for the period.

The Boring Company started inside SpaceX in 2017 and was spun out a year later. In September it raised $3 billion at a $23 billion valuation, with backing from the United Arab Emirates and other long-time Musk investors.

The tunnelling company has announced around a dozen city projects, but its only system open to the public today is the Las Vegas Convention Center Loop, which carries passengers in Tesla vehicles. Its largest active US build is the Music City Loop in Nashville, a planned link between downtown and the airport, and it plans more than 150 kilometres of tunnels in the UAE, including the Dubai Loop.

The same filing showed SpaceX bought $151 million of Tesla Megapack energy storage systems during the quarter.

news.title: Tesla Q4 updates: FSD delays, Optimus setbacks, and EV charging progress
news.summary: Tesla announced further delays for its Full Self-Driving (FSD) and Optimus robot, while competitors like Porsche and BMW made strides in EV charging innovation.
news.body:
Tesla has pushed back the release of its unsupervised Full Self-Driving (FSD) feature to Q2 2027, with the update only available within Robotaxi zones. This marks another delay in the feature’s development, which has been repeatedly postponed over the past several years. Additionally, the company has delayed the delivery of its Optimus humanoid robot to late 2027, citing ongoing challenges with its hands' functionality.

Despite these setbacks, Tesla reported a rebound in margins during its Q3 2026 financial results. However, the company’s overall profit still declined, and it has quietly reduced its 2026 capital expenditure guidance to $20 billion. Tesla also faced a 16% drop in energy revenue, attributed to customer refunds related to tariffs.

Meanwhile, competitors in the EV charging space have made notable advancements. Porsche has introduced wireless charging into production, while BMW demonstrated its iX5 model capable of up to 460 kW during a public fast-charging demo. Fortescue, in collaboration with KUKA, is utilizing welding robots to manage high-capacity 6 MW charging cables, signaling progress in addressing range anxiety.

These developments highlight Tesla’s ongoing challenges in delivering promised technologies, while other automakers and companies are making tangible progress in EV infrastructure.

news.title: Tesla Avoids Key Shareholder Question on HW3 Upgrade Plans
news.summary: Tesla skipped a major shareholder question about when Hardware 3 owners would receive a free computer upgrade for unsupervised Full Self-Driving during its Q3 2026 earnings call.
news.body:
During Tesla's Q3 2026 earnings call, the company skipped a top shareholder question regarding when Hardware 3 (HW3) owners would receive a free computer upgrade for the unsupervised 'Full Self-Driving' (FSD) feature they paid for. The question, which ranked fifth on the Say platform with 557 votes and 652,900 shares, was not addressed by Tesla's investor relations team, Travis Axelrod, despite being among the most upvoted queries.

The question asked: 'Tesla has acknowledged that HW3 vehicles cannot support unsupervised FSD. When will owners know whether they can upgrade their hardware for free, and when will Tesla provide a clear plan?' Tesla answered other questions about the Cybercab, robotaxi, and Optimus unit economics, but did not address the HW3 issue.

Tesla's head of AI, Ashok Elluswamy, did answer a related question about when unsupervised FSD would be available in customer cars. He stated that the same software running in Model Y robotaxis and the Cybercab would be available to customers with FSD v15, with the first customer vehicles joining the Robotaxi fleet 'somewhere around Q2 next year.' However, this timeline does not apply to HW3 vehicles, which Musk has previously stated lack the necessary hardware capabilities.

Tesla has faced legal challenges in the US, China, and Australia over the HW3 issue, with a Dutch collective claim involving nearly 7,000 owners. Documents show Tesla only submitted HW4 for FSD approval in Europe, while HW3 owners received a limited FSD v14 'Lite' version this year. The company has not provided a clear timeline or process for upgrading HW3 vehicles, despite previous promises from Musk about potential solutions like microfactories or next-gen boards.

The decision to skip the question has raised concerns about Tesla's transparency and legal exposure. Shareholders and owners are now left waiting for a resolution, with many questioning whether Tesla will ultimately honor its commitments to HW3 owners.

news.title: Tesla builds its own maps for FSD after years of rejecting them
news.summary: Tesla is developing its own maps to improve its Full Self-Driving system, marking a shift from its previous stance against relying on maps for autonomous driving.
news.body:
Tesla is now building its own maps to address recurring issues with its Full Self-Driving (FSD) system, including speed limit recognition, parking, and route selection. This change was revealed during Tesla’s Q3 2026 earnings call, where the company’s head of AI acknowledged the need to move away from third-party maps. The new system will use AI-based mapping and navigation, learning from the collective data of Tesla’s fleet and adapting to individual driver preferences.

The decision represents a notable shift for Tesla, which had previously dismissed the use of maps as unnecessary and overly complex. In 2019, Elon Musk described high-precision lane maps as a “huge mistake” and argued that self-driving could be achieved with cameras and AI alone. However, recent challenges with FSD’s ability to interpret basic road information, such as speed limit signs, have led the company to reconsider its approach.

Tesla’s new mapping system will initially handle the beginning and end of trips with FSD v15, with full navigation, parking, and destination handling expected in the following months. This approach mirrors that of Waymo, which uses its own fleet of vehicles to map cities and update them continuously. The key difference is that Waymo relies on lidar, while Tesla’s system is based on vision and AI.

The need for maps highlights a growing recognition that even advanced vision systems have limitations. Tesla’s fleet is now effectively acting as a mapping fleet, collecting data to improve the accuracy of its self-driving technology. This development brings Tesla closer to Waymo’s model, despite Musk’s earlier criticisms of the need for lidar and detailed maps.

As Tesla moves forward with its new mapping system, the company faces challenges in proving that its approach can reliably handle basic road information. The recent Belgian study showing FSD vehicles speeding in 30 km/h zones underscores the urgency of this change. With Tesla’s Robotaxi service operating in geofenced areas, the integration of its own maps may be a crucial step toward achieving a more reliable self-driving system.

news.title: Tesla pushes Optimus delivery to late 2027, citing hand and AI challenges
news.summary: Tesla has delayed Optimus humanoid robot deliveries to late 2027, citing ongoing issues with the robot's hands, durability, and AI capabilities.
news.body:
Tesla has pushed back the delivery of its Optimus humanoid robots to late 2027, according to Elon Musk during the company's Q3 2026 earnings call. The delay is attributed to unresolved challenges with the robot's hands, durability, and AI performance. Musk noted that these are common hurdles across the humanoid robotics industry, though he claimed no competitor is as close to Tesla's capabilities as he believes.

Tesla has begun early production of Optimus at its Fremont facility, which previously produced the Model S and Model X. The production line is designed for a million robots annually, but Musk acknowledged it will take at least a year, and possibly longer, to reach a rate of 20,000 units per week. This is due to ongoing design changes, particularly in the robot's hand and custom gear components.

The hand remains one of the most challenging hardware areas for Optimus. It must be soft enough to handle delicate objects while also being durable enough to withstand constant wear. Musk emphasized that the robot's AI architecture is also under development, as Tesla lacks the large fleet of robots needed to collect data in the same way its vehicles do for Full Self-Driving (FSD) capabilities. To address this, Tesla plans to build 10,000 to 20,000 robots for testing in an 'Optimus Academy.'

Musk also mentioned that Tesla will release a video within a month or two showcasing the robot performing unscripted tasks, aiming to demonstrate its real-world capabilities. However, the timeline for Optimus has repeatedly shifted, with previous goals of 2025 and 2026 now pushed to 2027.

Competitors such as XPeng and Boston Dynamics are also working on humanoid robots, with XPeng planning mass production of its IRON robot by the end of 2026 and Boston Dynamics already deploying its Atlas robot in a car factory. Despite Musk's claims of Tesla's lead, these companies are making progress with similar timelines.

Tesla's challenges with Optimus mirror those faced by other robotics companies, including the need for reliable hardware, robust AI, and practical applications. While Tesla has built a significant number of robots, the real challenge lies in making them useful and commercially viable.

news.title: Tesla plans Cybercab expansion to Dallas and sales to fleet operators
news.summary: Tesla says its Cybercab will launch in Dallas next month and more cities by year-end, and that it will start selling the vehicle to fleet operators before 2027.
news.body:
Tesla used its third-quarter earnings call to lay out an aggressive roll-out for the Cybercab, its two-seat autonomous vehicle with no steering wheel or pedals.

After starting in Austin, the Cybercab will expand to Dallas next month and to further cities by the end of the year. Tesla already runs smaller robotaxi fleets based on the Model Y in Dallas, Houston, Miami, Orlando and Tampa. CFO Vaibhav Taneja said the company's ambition is to own transportation of every kind on Earth.

Engineering vice president Lars Moravy said the Cybercabs built so far are all going into Tesla's own fleet, but that the company will begin delivering them to customers, starting with fleet operators, by year-end, and scale as it learns.

## Regulatory question mark

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration opened an investigation last month into how Tesla certified the Cybercab under federal safety standards, which still assume manual controls. The outcome could decide whether the vehicle can legally operate at scale. A Department of Transportation proposal to drop those requirements for self-driving vehicles is pending.

news.title: Tesla lowers 2026 capex guidance to $20B
news.summary: Tesla has revised its 2026 capital spending forecast downward from over $25 billion to more than $20 billion, signaling a shift in its financial strategy.
news.body:
Tesla has adjusted its 2026 capital expenditure (capex) guidance, reducing it from over $25 billion to more than $20 billion. This change was outlined in the company's Q3 10-Q filing, though not mentioned in its shareholder letter. The revision comes as Tesla reported $1.53 billion in positive free cash flow for the quarter, a figure heavily influenced by timing factors and accounting practices.

The company's capex guidance has fluctuated throughout the year. Initially set at around $20 billion, it was raised to over $25 billion in April, with CFO Vaibhav Taneja reaffirming the figure in July. However, the latest update brings it back to the original estimate. Tesla has already spent $13.01 billion in 2026, with $4.73 billion allocated in Q3 alone. To meet the previous $25 billion target, the company would have needed to spend nearly $12 billion in Q4, which is more than double its highest quarterly spending.

The 10-Q attributes the spending to initiatives like compute infrastructure, data centers, factory expansions, and company-operated assets. However, Tesla's actual spending is ahead of its reported cash capex, with $3.67 billion in equipment and construction liabilities as of September, up from $2.63 billion in June.

Tesla's Q3 free cash flow of $1.53 billion was driven by operating cash flow of $6.26 billion, which included $2.59 billion from changes in working capital. This figure was partly supported by accounts payable and accrued liabilities, including $722 million in unpaid purchases and $588 million in deferred revenue from SpaceX for undelivered Megapacks.

The capex reduction follows Tesla securing $30 billion in new credit facilities, including a $20 billion delayed-draw term loan and $10 billion in revolving credit. As of the end of Q3, Tesla had $45.4 billion in cash and investments, though it had not drawn on the new facilities.

The shift in capex guidance raises questions about whether Tesla is slowing its spending to preserve cash or if projects are being delayed into 2027. The company has not provided a clear explanation for the change, leaving investors to speculate on its implications for future growth and AI initiatives.

news.title: Tesla plans to sell Cybercab with no steering wheel by year-end
news.summary: Tesla announced plans to deliver the Cybercab to customers by the end of 2026, but the vehicle will lack a steering wheel and self-driving software until mid-2027.
news.body:
Tesla has announced its intention to deliver the Cybercab to consumers by the end of 2026. However, the vehicle will not include a steering wheel or fully autonomous driving software, raising questions about its usability during the initial period of ownership.

During Tesla’s Q3 earnings call, the company stated that unsupervised Full Self-Driving (FSD) software will be available to customers by mid-2027. This timeline marks a shift from previous estimates, which had placed the release of such technology further into the future. The Cybercab, however, is expected to reach customers by the end of 2026, according to VP of Engineering Lars Moravy.

The timeline raises concerns about the usability of the Cybercab during the six-month gap between its delivery and the availability of FSD software. Without a steering wheel or pedals, the vehicle would be inoperable for personal use, potentially limiting it to Tesla’s own Robotaxi fleet initially.

Tesla has also indicated that the Cybercab will be the first fully autonomous vehicle delivered to customers, with the company planning to scale its autonomous vehicle operations over time. However, the lack of immediate access to FSD software may limit the vehicle’s functionality in the short term.

Critics have questioned the practicality of this approach, noting that Tesla’s current Robotaxi fleet is limited in scope and that the Cybercab’s production may not meet demand. The company has not yet provided a clear explanation for the delay in making FSD software available to customers, despite having promised it for years.

news.title: Tesla delays unsupervised FSD to 2027, limited to Robotaxi zones
news.summary: Tesla has pushed the release of unsupervised Full Self-Driving (FSD) to Q2 2027, with the feature only available in limited Robotaxi zones.
news.body:
Tesla has announced that unsupervised Full Self-Driving (FSD) in customer-owned vehicles will not be available until Q2 2027. This update comes during Tesla’s Q3 2026 earnings call, where AI chief Ashok Elluswamy clarified that the feature will only be accessible within Tesla’s managed Robotaxi fleet, not as a standalone autonomous driving solution for personal use.

The timeline for FSD has been a long-standing promise from Elon Musk, dating back to 2016. However, Elluswamy emphasized that the first step is not a software update enabling personal autonomous travel, but rather allowing owners to add their cars to Tesla’s Robotaxi network. This means that unsupervised driving will only occur in areas where Tesla’s Robotaxi service is already operational.
